entries.title: I Corinthians 7:1
segments:
The things whereof ye wrote. The matters dealt with in this chapter, and others later, are treated in answer to written questions which the Corinthians had sent to the apostle.  The first question is concerning marriage and celibacy.  The frightful dissoluteness of the heathen society of the day led many earnest Christians to seek a remedy in the absolute separation of the sexes-a tendency which resulted in the vast number of hermits, monks, and nuns of a later period.
 

 
It is good for a man, etc.  It is well in view of the social conditions prevailing and the vicissitudes that were before the church at that period (
), a counsel of expediency, not a rule of duty.

entries.title: I Corinthians 7:21
segments: A bondservant. Slavery, which was part of the Roman political system in the apostle's time, and is impossible to abolish, is given as a strong instance to inculcate the doing of Christian duty in an existing relation.

segments: The distress that is upon us. The unsettled conditions of the times and of the rising church, with the probability of persecution-all viewed as part of the 'tribulation.'
